newsitem.title: CANADA: Oil output, margins lift Imperial Oil profits.
newsitem.headline: Oil output, margins lift Imperial Oil profits.

text.p: Imperial Oil Ltd., Canada's biggest energy company, on Tuesday reported a jump in second-quarter results, propelled by strong gains in heavy crude oil output and better refining and marketing margins.
But Toronto-based Imperial's first-half earnings were lower than last year because of a C$250 million ($183 million) one-time gain in 1996 after a major tax refund.

Imperial, 69 percent owned by U.S. oil giant Exxon Corp., reported second-quarter net earnings of C$183 million ($134 million), or C$1.18 (86 cents) a share, up 90 percent from year-earlier C$115 million ($84 million), or C62 cents (45 cents) a share.
Revenues rose to C$2.61 billion ($1.91 billion) from C$2.6 billion ($1.89 billion) in 1996.

First-half net earnings declined to C$379 million ($277 million), or C$2.39 ($1.74) a share, from last year's C$489 million ($357 million), or C$2.62 ($1.91) a share. Without the tax refund gain, Imperial's earnings per share in the first half of 1996 would have been C$1.41 ($1.03).
Revenues in the period climbed to C$5.29 billion ($3.86 billion) from C$4 billion ($2.92 billion) in 1996.
"These strong first-half results reflect improved operating performance and favorable market conditions in every segment of the business," Imperial Chairman Bob Peterson said in a statement.
